text: Which Excel function is the modern replacement for VLOOKUP, allowing for leftwards searches and exact matching by default?

options.A: XLOOKUP
options.D: LOOKUP

explanation: XLOOKUP is the modern lookup function that replaces VLOOKUP and HLOOKUP, supporting leftwards searches, exact matching by default, and wildcard options.

text: What is the purpose of the Excel function IFERROR?

options.A: It catches formula errors and returns a specified fallback value instead of the error code
options.B: It automatically highlights duplicate cells in a worksheet
options.C: It checks if the sheet contains blank formula inputs
options.D: It throws a warning popup to alert the user during data entry

explanation: IFERROR evaluates a formula; if it results in an error (e.g. #DIV/0!, #N/A), it returns a value you specify, preventing messy error tags.

text: Which function returns a value from a list based on a specified index position?

options.A: CHOOSE
options.D: VLOOKUP

explanation: CHOOSE(index_num, value1, value2, ...) returns a specific value from the list argument based on the position index_num.

text: What is the difference between XLOOKUP and VLOOKUP when a lookup value is not found?

options.A: XLOOKUP has a built-in 'if_not_found' argument; VLOOKUP requires wrapping with IFERROR
options.C: XLOOKUP only works on text; VLOOKUP only works on numbers
options.D: There is no difference; both return #N/A without alternatives

explanation: XLOOKUP includes a fourth optional parameter (if_not_found) that specifies what to return if no match is found, eliminating extra wrapper functions.

text: Which formula combines INDEX and MATCH to find a value at the intersection of a specific row and column?

options.A: INDEX(range, MATCH(), MATCH())
options.D: INDEX(range, MATCH())

explanation: The syntax INDEX(array, row_num, column_num) uses one MATCH function for row_num and a second MATCH for column_num to perform a two-way lookup.

text: What feature restricts the values that a user can input into a cell (e.g. integer between 1 and 10)?

options.A: Data Validation
options.D: AutoFilter

explanation: Data Validation limits cell inputs based on rules you define, such as numbers, dates, or items from a list.

text: How can you automatically change the fill color of a cell to red if its value is less than 50?

options.A: Conditional Formatting
options.D: Cell Styles

explanation: Conditional Formatting dynamically changes a cell's appearance (font color, fill, border) based on rules evaluated against its value.

text: How do you create a drop-down list of options in a cell?

options.A: Data Validation -> Allow: List -> Source: Select range of options
options.C: Format Cells -> Protection -> Allow dropdown options
options.D: Developer tab -> Insert combo box control

explanation: Setting Data Validation to 'List' and providing a comma-separated text or cell range source creates an in-cell drop-down arrow.

text: What does a green triangle in the top-left corner of an Excel cell indicate?

options.A: An error checking warning (e.g. number stored as text, formula omission)
options.B: The cell is locked and protected from edits
options.C: The cell is actively linked to another worksheet
options.D: A macro is running on the cell in the background

explanation: Excel places a green triangle in a cell to warn of potential errors, like a formula that differs from adjacent ones or numeric data formatted as text.

text: Which conditional formatting type displays horizontal bars inside cells representing their values relative to other cells?

options.A: Data Bars
options.D: Sparklines

explanation: Data Bars are inline formatting visualizers where the length of the bar represents the cell's numeric value relative to other cells in the range.

text: What are Sparklines in Excel?

options.A: Miniature charts placed inside a single cell representing a row or column of data
options.B: Flashing borders around cells that contain formula errors
options.C: Lines connecting related shapes in a flow diagram
options.D: Formulas that dynamically filter data using search keywords

explanation: Sparklines are tiny, simple charts embedded in a cell to show trends or patterns in adjacent numerical data.

text: Which chart type is best for showing a comparison of values across categories in a horizontal layout?

options.A: Bar chart
options.D: Pie chart

explanation: Bar charts are oriented horizontally, whereas Column charts are oriented vertically. Horizontal bar charts are ideal when labels are long.

text: What is the purpose of adding a 'Trendline' to an Excel scatter chart?

options.A: To show the general direction or pattern of the data points mathematically
options.B: To connect the dots sequentially using a zig-zag line path
options.C: To highlight the highest and lowest points on the visual
options.D: To divide the chart area into separate quadrants

explanation: Trendlines visualize data trends and can calculate regression equations (linear, exponential, etc.) across scatter or line plots.

text: Which element acts as a visual map of the colors and markers used in a chart?

options.A: Legend
options.D: Gridline

explanation: The Legend lists the labels and key indicators representing different data series on the chart.

text: How do you add a secondary axis to a chart in Excel?

options.A: Change Chart Type -> Combo -> Check 'Secondary Axis' box for a series
options.B: Double-click the chart background and select 'Duplicate Y-Axis'
options.C: Insert a second separate chart directly on top of the first one
options.D: Drag the numerical field to the Columns area

explanation: Combo charts support plotting a series on a secondary Y-axis, which is necessary when metrics have different ranges (e.g. counts vs percentages).

text: What is a 'structured reference' in Excel?

options.A: Referencing data using table and column names instead of cell coordinates (e.g. Table1[Sales])
options.B: A formula that is locked using the dollar sign absolute indicator ($A$1)
options.C: An external link to cells in a closed workbook file
options.D: A macro script that automatically sorts rows

explanation: Structured references use the table name and column headers to make formulas readable and self-adjusting as rows are added.

text: How do you quickly format a range of cells as an official Excel Table?

options.A: Home -> Format as Table (or press Ctrl + T)
options.B: Insert -> Border styles -> All borders option
options.D: Data -> Data Tools -> Table layout

explanation: Ctrl + T (or Home -> Format as Table) converts a data range into a table with active filtering, structured references, and banded rows.

text: What happens to a structured reference formula like SUM(Sales[Amount]) when a new row is added to the table?

options.A: The formula automatically updates to include the new row value
options.B: The formula breaks and returns a #REF! error
options.C: The user must edit the range manually in the formula bar
options.D: Excel creates a duplicate formula cell automatically

explanation: Excel tables are dynamic; structured references automatically expand or shrink to include new rows added to columns.

text: Which table feature adds an automatic sum, average, or count row at the bottom of the table?

options.A: Total Row
options.D: Grand Total layout

explanation: Enabling the 'Total Row' in Table Design adds a row at the bottom with dropdown menus to choose aggregation functions for each column.

text: What is the difference between filtering a table and sorting a table?

options.A: Filtering hides rows that do not meet criteria; sorting changes the display order of rows
options.B: Sorting deletes data; filtering only duplicates cells
options.C: Filtering is temporary; sorting is a permanent action that cannot be undone
options.D: There is no difference; they perform the same actions

explanation: Sorting rearranges data alphabetically or numerically. Filtering hides rows based on criteria without altering row order.

text: What language is used to write and execute macros in Microsoft Excel?

options.A: VBA (Visual Basic for Applications)
options.D: SQL query scripts

explanation: Excel macros are written and stored in the VBA programming language, managed using the built-in VBA Editor.

text: How do you create a simple macro without writing code manually?

options.A: Use the 'Record Macro' button in the Developer ribbon
options.B: Write Excel formulas in a text file and rename it
options.C: Link Excel to an external database script
options.D: Double-click the cells while holding the Alt key

explanation: The Macro Recorder captures mouse clicks and keystrokes, translating them into VBA code automatically.

text: What file extension must you use to save an Excel workbook that contains macros?

options.A: .xlsm
options.D: .csv

explanation: The standard .xlsx format strips out macros. To preserve macros, you must save the workbook as Excel Macro-Enabled Workbook (.xlsm).

text: Which tab in Excel contains macro commands, XML options, and Form Controls?

options.A: Developer
options.D: Insert

explanation: The Developer tab is hidden by default and houses VBA, Macros, Add-ins, and form controls. It can be enabled in options.

text: What is the danger of enabling all macros in Excel security settings?

options.A: Malicious code within external workbooks could execute automatically, compromising security
options.B: Excel will crash immediately due to memory overflow errors
options.C: It prevents the use of basic formulas like SUM and AVERAGE
options.D: It permanently encrypts the workbook using a random key

explanation: Macros have full access to your operating system. Running unverified macros can lead to malware infection or data theft.

text: Which What-If Analysis tool is best when you know the desired output of a formula but not the input value required?

options.A: Goal Seek
options.D: Solver Add-in

explanation: Goal Seek is a built-in tool that adjusts a single input cell until a dependent formula cell reaches a target value.

text: What What-If Analysis tool allows you to save and switch between multiple sets of input values in a worksheet?

options.A: Scenario Manager
options.D: Solver

explanation: Scenario Manager allows users to store multiple scenarios (e.g. Best Case, Worst Case) and swap inputs with a click.

text: What is the difference between Goal Seek and the Solver add-in?

options.A: Goal Seek changes only one input variable; Solver can optimize multiple input variables with constraints
options.B: Solver is for charts; Goal Seek is only for formulas
options.C: Goal Seek is an external download; Solver is built-in by default
options.D: There is no difference; Solver is the newer name for Goal Seek

explanation: Goal Seek solves single-variable equations. Solver is a linear optimization tool that handles complex constraints and multiple variables.

text: How do you enable the Solver add-in in Excel?

options.A: File -> Options -> Add-ins -> Manage: Excel Add-ins -> Check 'Solver Add-in'
options.B: Insert -> Chart tools -> Select Solver icon
options.C: Right-click the formula bar and select 'Enable Solver'
options.D: Download the solver.exe file from the Windows Store

explanation: Solver is packaged with Excel but inactive by default. It must be turned on in the Excel Add-ins management window.

text: Which What-If analysis tool displays the results of changing one or two inputs directly in a grid layout?

options.A: Data Table
options.D: Solver

explanation: A Data Table calculates a formula range for values listed in rows/columns, plotting results in a matrix view.

text: What does a cell containing '###' indicate in Excel?

options.A: The column is too narrow to display the formatted number value
options.B: The cell contains a division by zero error formula
options.C: The cell is locked and protected from edits
options.D: The formula contains invalid circular reference links

explanation: When numeric or date values exceed the column width, Excel prints '###'. Double-clicking the border column auto-fits it.

text: How can you sort a list of dates chronologically from oldest to newest?

options.A: Sort & Filter -> Sort Oldest to Newest
options.D: Developer -> Custom Sort -> Date format only

explanation: Sort & Filter options detect date data types, offering oldest-to-newest or newest-to-oldest chronological sorts.

text: What is a 'Custom Sort' in Excel?

options.A: Sorting data based on a custom list (e.g. High, Medium, Low) instead of alphabetical order
options.B: A macro script that sorts rows randomly
options.C: Sorting cells by their text length counts
options.D: A filter that only displays colored cells

explanation: Custom Sort allows sorting by custom lists (like sizes: S, M, L, XL) or sorting multiple levels (e.g. by Department, then Surname).

text: What feature enables filtering data columns based on text parameters (e.g. 'Contains', 'Begins With')?

options.A: Text Filters
options.D: Cell styles

explanation: Clicking the filter arrow on a text column opens Text Filters options to search containing, matching, or starting characters.

text: Which wildcard character represents any number of characters in Excel filter searches?

options.A: Asterisk (*)
options.D: Ampersand (&)

explanation: The asterisk (*) acts as a wildcard representing zero or more characters in lookups and search filters.

text: How do you prevent users from editing specific cells while allowing edits in others?

options.A: Unlock allowed cells, then protect the worksheet
options.B: Lock the allowed cells, then save the file
options.C: Apply conditional formatting to block input focus
options.D: Set Data Validation on all cells to allow nothing

explanation: All cells are locked by default. You must select allowed cells, uncheck 'Locked' in Format Cells -> Protection, then enable Sheet Protection.

text: What is the difference between Protecting a Worksheet and Protecting a Workbook?

options.A: Worksheet protection locks cells; Workbook protection locks structure (preventing adding/deleting sheets)
options.B: Workbook protection is paid; Worksheet protection is free
options.C: Protecting a workbook converts the file into a read-only PDF format
options.D: There is no difference; they are duplicate terms

explanation: Worksheet protection restricts cell edits. Workbook protection prevents structural changes like inserting, deleting, or renaming tabs.

text: How do you encrypt an Excel file with a password so it cannot be opened without authorization?

options.A: File -> Info -> Protect Workbook -> Encrypt with Password
options.B: Review -> Protect Sheet -> Input Password option
options.D: Save As -> CSV format -> Select Encryption keys

explanation: Encryption uses password protection to encrypt the entire file container, blocking unauthenticated reading/opening of the file.

text: Where is the option to protect a sheet located in the default Excel ribbons?

options.A: Review tab
options.D: Insert tab

explanation: The 'Protect Sheet' and 'Protect Workbook' commands are located in the Protect group on the Review tab.

text: What does checking the 'Lock Cell' box in Format Cells -> Protection do if the worksheet is NOT protected?

options.A: Nothing; cell locks are only active when sheet protection is enabled
options.D: It turns the background color of the cell gray

explanation: Locking or hiding cells has no effect until you actively protect the worksheet (Review -> Protect Sheet).
